I DELETED ANOTHER PROJECT'S ROOTED FILE FROM THE LEDGER AND RESTORED IT -- the deletion guard's override is what let it through, and 'verify then commit' did not catch it. FIFTH mode of the shared-index hazard.
MISATTRIBUTION, not data loss: commit c752d200f2 carries my message over ANOTHER LANE'S FILE. Nothing is lost; the ledger's authorship is wrong for two paths.

A SHARED INDEX CAN BE CLEARED BETWEEN YOUR add AND YOUR commit, so the commit reports 'no changes added' while your work is ALREADY at HEAD under another lane's message -- and the two failure modes look identical from your side
I DID I-1041/I-1055 TO ajc-p2, WITH ONE EXPLICIT PATH AND A CLEAN-LOOKING INDEX -- and the pre-commit 'git diff --cached' check that would have caught it is the one nobody runs BEFORE staging
THE SHARED-INDEX HAZARD HAS A FOURTH MODE: THE INDEX CAN CHANGE BETWEEN YOUR VERIFICATION AND YOUR COMMIT, so 'git diff --cached' immediately before committing is STILL not sufficient.

ANTECEDENT 2 IS NOT WEAKENED BY RESTRICTION AT ALL: coverage at ANY V implies UNRESTRICTED coverage, and the same fact shuts the bot instance-binder loophole.
DELETE THE GEOMETRY AND RE-PROVE THE CLAIM: an order-theoretic skeleton tells you which hypotheses the theorem actually used, and the docstring is usually crediting the wrong one.

nested_iff_shared IS REAL WORK BUT ITS "SQUEEZE" REASON IS FALSE (EITHER monotonicity ALONE suffices), IT SITS ONE LEVEL BELOW THE ASSEMBLY IT RETIRES, AND THE HEADER CITES A DECLARATION OUTSIDE ITS IMPORT CLOSURE.
THE FILE'S SELF-DECLARED "SUBSTANTIVE CONTENT" IS ONE rfl PLUS ONE MATHLIB LEMMA, AND ITS DOCSTRING MISDESCRIBES ITS OWN PROOF: iso-ness of topIso is never used.
SHARING A BINDER IS NOT COUPLING -- check the two hypotheses MONOTONICITY in the shared parameter before pricing them as inseparable.
Atlas-coupling: the coverage witness must land in a V CONTAINED IN the one hf is certified at -- and the nesting buys nothing
